title: Picosecond-resolved entanglement distribution over an urban free-space channel
authors: Alessandro Laneve, Fabrizio Cienzo, Santiago Gomez, Paolo Barigelli, Philip Menz, Mattia Beccaceci, Giuseppe Ronco, Giorgia Grossi, Ievgen Brytavskyi, Thomas Oberleitner, Markus Wiener, Christian Weidinger, Tobias M. Krieger, Ailton Garcia, Saimon Filipe Covre da Silva, Michele B. Rota, Nicolò Spagnolo, Henning Weier, Fabio Sciarrino, Armando Rastelli, Rinaldo Trotta
abstract: Time-evolving entangled states describe quantum particles whose correlations evolve in time according to a well-defined dynamics. Such states can be generated in a variety of physical systems and are promising resources for several quantum technologies, ranging from quantum clock synchronization to quantum communication. However, their full potential is currently limited by the fact that the entanglement dynamics often occur on timescales comparable to the achievable synchronization precision, especially in experiments aimed at distributing entanglement through noisy urban channels. In this context, accurate timing is not merely a technical detail, but a fundamental requirement for faithfully observing and exploiting the underlying quantum correlations. Here, we demonstrate the faithful distribution of a fast-evolving entangled state over a 270 m free-space channel connecting two buildings in the center of Rome. The developed system incorporates a synchronization device capable of achieving sub-50 ps timing accuracy between the two ends of the link while simultaneously supporting channel stabilization. Our results demonstrate that time-evolving entanglement can be reliably transmitted through a noisy urban free-space channel, representing an important benchmark toward long-distance free-space quantum communication and the future implementation of time-correlated entangled states in demanding scenarios such as satellite-based quantum networks.
summary: The research demonstrates the reliable transmission of time-evolving entangled states over a challenging 270 m urban free-space channel. By implementing a high-precision synchronization system achieving sub-50 ps jitter, the authors maintained high entanglement fidelity and even benchmarked secure key generation rates. This work establishes a crucial experimental milestone for long-distance quantum communication.
main_problem: The primary goal was to demonstrate the faithful distribution of fast-evolving entangled quantum states over a noisy, long-distance free-space optical channel.
main_result: The authors successfully transmitted time-evolving entanglement across 270 m in an urban setting, achieving high fidelity (up to 89% FEF) by implementing advanced synchronization techniques.
method: The experiment utilized a quantum dot source generating entangled photon pairs and incorporated a novel laser-based synchronization device to maintain sub-50 ps timing accuracy over the free-space link.
model_or_system: The system uses an entangled two-photon state generated via biexciton-exciton cascades in a Quantum Dot (QD) source. The transmission channel is a 270 m free-space link connecting buildings in Rome, requiring precise time synchronization for measurement.
key_observables: Time-resolved degree of entanglement (FEF), fidelity to the target state $|\phi^+angle$, and Secure Key Fraction (SKF) for QKD benchmarking.
important_parameters: Sub-50 ps timing jitter, 270 m channel distance, oscillation periods on hundreds of picoseconds.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that time-wise post-selection is necessary to mitigate noise and maintain quantum correlations over the noisy link; the protocol relies heavily on low temporal jitter between remote parties.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup scheme, the synchronization device components, and quantitative comparisons of entanglement fidelity (FEF) achieved in both laboratory settings versus the free-space channel.
paper_structure: The paper details the physical system (QD source), introduces the challenge of timing over noisy channels, presents the novel synchronization method, validates the transmission of time-evolving entanglement via high FEF measurements, and finally benchmarks its potential for secure quantum key distribution.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the critical engineering bottleneck—timing stability—for scaling quantum communication from controlled lab environments to real-world, noisy free-space links, which is fundamental for future quantum networks.
